accepted.summary: The course explores how AI-powered tools—IDEs, terminals, code review and testing platforms—are reshaping the software development life cycle. It connects core principles of building complex systems with hands-on experience using state-of-the-art AI tools, delivered through real-world engineering tasks and a team-based project guided by industry practitioners.
learning_outcomes: Learn how to use the latest AI-powered workflows
Understand when and why to trust AI tools in software development
Develop skills and perspective to thrive in the era of AI-driven development
prerequisites: Courses listed in the prerequisites (specific courses not named on this page)
accepted.pedagogy_notes: Real-world engineering tasks and a team-based project; guided by industry pioneers.
evidence_quotes: AI is rapidly transforming how we build, debug, and maintain software.
From new-age IDEs and terminals like Cursor and Warp to code review and testing platforms like Coderabbit and Qodo
Through real-world engineering tasks and a team-based project
If you have not taken the courses listed in the prerequisites but believe you have equivalent experience
accepted.relevance_reason: Matches TG1 (AI-assisted coding, developer workflows) and TG6 (emerging developer tools, projects); partially touches TG5 (testing platforms). Missing TG2 (agentic engineering, MCP, context engineering), TG3 (spec-driven development), and TG4 (loop engineering, software factories).

accepted.course_title: AI-Augmented Research and Development: Foundations and Practice
accepted.summary: This graduate-level course teaches students how to integrate AI tools into scientific research with rigor, treating large language models and prompting as an engineering discipline. It covers retrieval-augmented generation, AI-assisted software development, agentic systems, human-AI collaboration, and evaluation frameworks, culminating in a capstone project. [EXTERNAL]
topics: evaluation frameworks for detecting and analyzing Al failures
accepted.pedagogy_notes: Students build working systems on their own research data throughout the course, culminating in a capstone project that produces a deliverable for their research group.
evidence_quotes: EE 292M: AI-Augmented Research and Development: Foundations and Practice
Al-Augmented Research teaches graduate students to integrate Al tools into scientific research with the same rigor they apply to experimental design and statistical inference.
It teaches retrieval-augmented generation, Al-assisted software development, agentic systems, human-Al collaboration patterns, and evaluation frameworks for detecting and analyzing Al failures.
accepted.relevance_reason: Matches AI-assisted software development and agentic systems, but focuses on scientific research rather than general software engineering workflows and spec-driven development.

accepted.summary: This NUS module introduces students to generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools and their impact across diverse domains. It equips learners to use curated GAI tools effectively in academic and professional contexts while critically examining associated societal challenges. The course emphasizes practical engagement with these tools through discussions and projects.
evidence_quotes: CP1008: Learning with Generative AI Tools
Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools are set to make a profound impact across many fields including business, science, music, art and literature.
Students will also critique various societal issues associated with GAI tools.
accepted.relevance_reason: The module addresses AI tool usage and societal implications, aligning with AI‑assisted coding and tool‑use aspects of the target course, but lacks coverage of specification, testing, and iterative development workflows.

accepted.summary: The course provides conceptual and analytical tools for systematic software development, emphasizing object‑oriented analysis, modelling, design, implementation and testing. It teaches UML, program specification and testing methods, and discusses modularisation, correctness and software quality.

evidence_quotes: This course introduces the necessary conceptual and analytical tools for systematic and rigorous development of software systems.
It covers four main areas of software development, namely object-oriented system analysis, object-oriented system modelling and design, implementation, and testing.
Tools and techniques for software development, such as Unified Modelling Language (UML), program specification, and testing methods, will be taught.
